messages:

Cc: priya.desai@veloria.com, chuck.reynolds@veloria.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Private deploy runbook + egress checklist (Veloria)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We want to schedule a dry-run of the on-prem installer and VPC peering steps next week ahead of the production cutover. Primary asks before the dry-run:

- Confirm required outbound egress ranges (we need this for our firewall change window).
- Share the exact installer manifest and expected hostnames/IPs for private endpoints.
- Walk us through the KV cache migration step so we can validate data residency.

Can your team do a 60–90 min dry-run on Tue 24 Jul or Wed 25 Jul (US-Eastern)? Prefer morning.

Attaching our internal network diagram and the initial SOW questions.

—Alex
Network Ops | Veloria Therapeutics
attachments: veloria_network_overview.pdf (pdf)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@veloria.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 17:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private deploy runbook + egress checklist (Veloria)

Alex — thanks, and great to meet the team last week. We can run the dry-run and egress validation. Proposed plan:

1) Preflight (45m): review egress ranges, certs, and the installer manifest.
2) Dry-run (45m): run the on-prem installer in staging, validate private endpoints and KV swap.
3) Post-check (15m): confirm cutover checklist and action items.

Availability: Tue 24 Jul 09:30–11:30 ET or Wed 25 Jul 10:00–12:00 ET. Please confirm preferred slot.

Marcus will lead the installer walkthrough and Kim will own the networking preflight checklist. I will coordinate invites and test accounts.

Quick note on materials we’ll send before the call:
- installer_manifest_v1.2.yaml (expected env vars and toggles)
- veloria_vpc_diagram.png (Redwood annotated)
- preflight-checklist.pdf (what we validate live)

If you share any hostnames that must be whitelisted ahead of time, we’ll call those out in the invite.

—Soojin
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@veloria.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy runbook + egress checklist (Veloria)

Alex / team — adding a few technical clarifications so you can prep the staging hosts: 

- Installer: the manifest we share requires SSH access from the staging runner to each target host (key-based). We can also run via jump-host if you prefer.
- Egress: outbound token validation and model-fetch callouts go to these CIDR blocks: 34.120.0.0/14, 52.23.96.0/19, and 198.51.100.0/24. If you have a strict egress policy we can route via our relay in us-east-1.
- HSM/KMS: if you plan to use customer-managed keys, include the KMS ARN in the manifest and ensure IAM permissions for the service account.

Marcus will demo the KV cache warmup and the fallback behavior when prefix caching is enabled. Expect a 10–15s token delay in staging when we do the first warmup pass.

Also dropping the installer manifest and an annotated VPC diagram to the Drive link so you can pull them ahead of the dry-run.

—Marcus
Sr. Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: installer_manifest_v1.2.yaml (yaml)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@veloria.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 08:41:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private deploy runbook + egress checklist (Veloria)

Alex — adding the preflight checklist here for visibility. Highlights for your networking team: 

- DNS: private endpoint hostnames must resolve to the private IPs provided in the manifest. Test with dig + short TTL.
- MTU: ensure your appliances have an MTU >= 1400 to avoid fragmentation with gRPC streams.
- Route tables: add a route for the redwood-managed relay subnet during the dry-run if you choose relay mode.
- Firewall: allow outbound to the CIDRs Marcus listed and open ports 443 and 8443 for the installer API.
- Monitoring: we’ll instrument a short trace and a token-latency baseline for the session; please provide an admin user for the staging cluster.

Attached: preflight-checklist.pdf (PDF) and a one-page egress summary.

If the 24 Jul 09:30 ET slot works, we’ll send calendar invites and pre-reqs (SSH key, staging admin account).

—Kimberly
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
attachments: preflight-checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@veloria.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: priya.desai@veloria.com, chuck.reynolds@veloria.com

Subject: Re: Private deploy runbook + egress checklist (Veloria)

Thanks all — Tue 24 Jul 09:30 ET works for Veloria. Agenda confirmed.

Action items from Veloria before the dry-run: 
- We’ll provide the staging admin account and a temporary SSH key by EOD Mon 23 Jul.
- Chuck will open the firewall windows for the CIDRs you listed.
- Priya (security) will upload the KMS ARN if we decide to run with customer-managed keys.

We reviewed the Drive folder and see the manifest and checklist. I’ll also raise VEL-341 in Jira for a follow-up on egress logging.

One more ask — for audit/compliance we need a signed statement on data retention behavior for the staging run (short, 1–2 lines) and a DocuSign link for the SOW addendum. If you can drop that before the session we can attach to the ticket.

Thanks — see you Tuesday.

—Alex
Network Ops | Veloria Therapeutics
